PERSONAL PORTFOLIO LANDING PAGE
New Audit

PDF

34
OVERALL VERDICT
"Well-packaged metadata is hiding a page that is effectively empty to both users and search engines."

The page has several good technical basics in place: HTTPS, canonical, viewport, Open Graph tags, and Person schema. But the core product problem is severe: the fetched page exposes virtually no visible content, no headings, no links, no calls to action, and no navigational structure. That makes it weak as a portfolio, poor at converting visitors, and at risk of underperforming in search because Google has almost nothing substantive to index beyond the title and meta description.

34
SCORE
SEO Audit
11 / 16 ON-PAGE CHECKS PASSING

The page meets several basic technical SEO requirements: it returns HTTP 200, is indexable, uses HTTPS, and includes a valid title, meta description, canonical, viewport, and Person schema. But the biggest issue is content: rendered word count is just 6, visible text is effectively empty, there is no H1, and there are zero internal or external links. In Google's people-first framework, the page currently does not deliver useful, indexable content matching the promise of "AI/ML Engineering Student," so metadata is doing almost all the work. There is no evidence of spam-policy violations, but there are important crawl and discoverability gaps such as missing robots.txt and sitemap.xml.

SEO ISSUES
og:image needs attention
INFO

og:image is 1024x576px — below the recommended 1200x630 for large summary cards.

Fix: Serve a reachable og:image at 1200x630 (600x315 minimum for non-large cards) and keep it under ~1MB for fast social unfurls.
No robots.txt found
INFO

A robots.txt was not found at the site root. Crawlers cannot discover crawl rules or a sitemap reference.

Fix: Add a /robots.txt that allows crawling of public pages and includes a `Sitemap:` line pointing to your sitemap.xml.
No valid sitemap.xml found
INFO

A valid XML sitemap was not found at /sitemap.xml. Sitemaps help search engines discover and prioritize your pages.

Fix: Generate a sitemap.xml (a `<urlset>` of your public URLs) and reference it from robots.txt.
Address mismatch (NAP inconsistency)
WARNING

The postal address in structured data does not appear in the visible page text. Consistent name/address/phone is a key local-SEO signal.

Fix: Ensure the structured-data PostalAddress matches the address displayed on the page and across directory listings.
Physical address without LocalBusiness schema
INFO

The page shows a physical address but has no LocalBusiness (or subtype) JSON-LD, so search engines cannot reliably associate the location with the business.

Fix: Add LocalBusiness JSON-LD with name, address, telephone, geo, and openingHours to strengthen local-SEO eligibility.
Add meaningful indexable body content
CRITICAL

Google can index the page, but there is almost nothing to index: rendered word count is 6 and the visible text is effectively blank. This fails the Search Essentials requirement that a page contain actual indexable content.

Fix: Publish visible page copy that matches the topic promised by the title and meta description: add an H1, a short intro, project summaries, skills, and contact details directly in HTML on the page.
Add a clear H1 that matches page intent
WARNING

The page has 0 H1s, 0 H2s, and 0 H3s. Without a visible page heading, both users and search engines lack a strong on-page cue for what the page actually is.

Fix: Add a visible H1 near the top such as "Tushar Kapoor — AI/ML Engineering Student" or "Tushar Kapoor Portfolio," then support it with section headings like Projects, Skills, and Contact.
Add internal links to portfolio destinations
WARNING

The page has 0 internal links and 0 external links. That leaves the homepage as a dead end and gives Google no paths to crawl related project or resume content.

Fix: Add internal links to sections or subpages such as /projects, /resume, and /contact, using descriptive anchor text like "View IoT sensor pipeline project" instead of generic labels.
Align snippet source with the meta description
WARNING

The meta description is strong, but Google often builds snippets from visible page text. Because the body has essentially no opening copy, search results may fall back to poor or rewritten snippets.

Fix: Write the first 1-2 visible sentences on the page to mirror the real value proposition, for example: "I build AI/ML and IoT projects focused on real-world sensing, deep learning, and algorithmic problem solving."
Publish robots.txt and sitemap.xml
INFO

robots.txt returns 404 and sitemap.xml returns 404. These are not required for ranking, but they help search engines discover and monitor a growing site efficiently.

Fix: Add a root robots.txt that allows crawling and references sitemap.xml, then publish a sitemap containing the homepage and any project/detail pages.
Add Twitter card metadata
INFO

Open Graph tags are present, but Twitter card tags are missing. This does not affect Google rankings directly, but it weakens share previews that can drive secondary discovery and links.

Fix: Add twitter:card, twitter:title, twitter:description, and twitter:image tags matching the existing Open Graph values.
Upgrade the Open Graph image size
INFO

The OG image is valid and fetched successfully, but it is 1024x576, below the recommended 1200x630 for large summary cards. This can reduce visual quality in shared previews.

Fix: Export a 1200x630 version of the portfolio preview image and update og:image to that asset.
SEO OPPORTUNITIES
Build project pages around real AI/ML topics
HIGH EFFORT

Create dedicated pages for each substantive project tied to the themes already named in metadata: applied AI, deep learning, IoT sensor pipelines, and algorithmic problem solving. Each page should explain the problem, approach, stack, and outcome so the site can rank for topic-specific long-tail searches rather than only your name.

Impact: This would expand the site from a branded placeholder into a discoverable topical portfolio.
Turn the homepage into a search-friendly portfolio hub
MEDIUM EFFORT

Use the homepage to summarize who you are, what domains you work in, and where each project lives. This gives Google a stronger overview page and helps users navigate quickly to the most relevant evidence of your skills.

Impact: A stronger hub page will improve relevance for branded queries and increase crawl flow to deeper pages.
Add visible proof signals for expertise
MEDIUM EFFORT

Include concrete artifacts such as project outcomes, technologies used, coursework, publications, certifications, GitHub links, or internship work where applicable. For a portfolio, specificity matters more than generic claims like "algorithmic problem solving."

Impact: More specific proof points will strengthen content quality and improve click-through from people evaluating your credibility.
Expand Person schema with sameAs and profile links
LOW EFFORT

You already have Person JSON-LD, so enrich it with links to GitHub, LinkedIn, email, and any public profiles that represent the same person. This helps search engines connect your identity across the web and understand the site as an authoritative personal profile.

Impact: Stronger entity clarity can improve how your branded presence is interpreted in search.
Local SEO

5
Collect and respond to reviews on Google and relevant industry directories.

AI in use
MEDIUM CONFIDENCE

The site presents AI as part of the subject matter and personal brand rather than as an observable product feature. The strongest evidence is in the page copy and metadata referencing "AI/ML," "Applied AI," and "deep learning," but there is no evidence of live AI functionality, models, or vendors powering the site experience itself.
